textNichtAktiv: The adapter is not running. Live values, lists and every button that asks the adapter (search, read, check, test) only work after it has been started (▶ at the top). Settings can still be changed and saved.
helpPort: Port the broker listens on. Must differ from any other MQTT broker (e.g. the mqtt adapter).
helpUser: Optional. Empty = modules connect without login. If set, the modules must use the same credentials (module settings mqttuser / mqttpass) – "Connect" in the tab "Find modules" writes them into the module for you.
helpPass: Stored encrypted. Only used if a user name is set.
textSetup: Open the module's web interface, go to Settings, tab Basic, and set 'MQTT host' to <ioBroker IP>:<port above>. The module reconnects on its own.
textDocker: The broker port must be published by the container, otherwise the modules cannot reach it. Add a port mapping for the port configured above.
textLive: By default a module reports its status every 60 seconds ('reporting'), so a command is confirmed only with the next report. Enabling 'livestatus' in the module's Extra settings makes it report immediately.
textConsumption: The units only report lifetime counters. The adapter derives hourly and daily consumption from them (consumption.*), keeps the totals unchanged (status.*) and stores the last 48 hours as JSON for the widget.
labelHistoryRegister: Log consumption with the history adapter
helpHistoryRegister: Registers the consumption data points for recording automatically, so charts work without configuring each point by hand.
headerModule: For advanced users: Settings in the faikout module for the complete set of data points
textModule: Which data points appear depends on settings in the faikout module itself (web interface of the module, Settings; most of them under Advanced; older firmware spells them without the dot, e.g. 'haenable'). Nothing has to be set here in the adapter.
setOtherNo: other no.* (econo, powerful, comfort, streamer, quiet, sensor, swingv, swingh, flap, antifreeze)
effMqttHost: Connects the module to this adapter's broker.
effHaEnable: Required. Only with it does the module publish its readings (temperatures, mode, energy …); without it only diagnostics arrive and the adapter logs a warning.
effFanRpm: Fan speed (status.fanfreq) in rpm instead of Hz. The adapter detects the unit itself; rpm is more precise.
effCompRpm: Compressor speed (status.comp) in rpm instead of Hz. The adapter detects the unit itself.
effSwitches: Adds status.autoe, the main switch of the module's own automation.
effHvacAction: Adds status.action: what the unit is actually doing (heating, cooling, idle, defrosting …).
effHumidity: Humidity status.hum. Switch it on only if the unit has no humidity sensor.
effLed: LED control control.led - only if the unit's display LED can be switched.
effHumidify: Humidifier control control.humidify - only for units with a humidifier.
effOtherNo: Each one hides the matching function. Switch on only for functions your unit really lacks.
effLivestatus: Reports immediately instead of every 'reporting' seconds, so commands are confirmed within about a second.
effReporting: Interval of the periodic report in seconds.
textModuleNoSetting: No setting is needed for energy counters, power draw, compressor and fan speed, refrigerant and outside temperature: the module reads them from the unit on its own. Whether they appear depends only on the model.
textModulSofort: Everything in this section goes straight to the module: “Write to module” takes effect at once. “Save” at the bottom is not needed for it (it only becomes active because the form has been filled in).
textSearchAddress: The modules connect to this address and the broker port. It is pre-filled from the network interfaces of this host. In Docker only the address of the Docker host works - enter it here.
labelModuleAddress: Address for modules (IP or host name)
helpModuleAddress: Address of the ioBroker host as seen by the modules
errorModuleAddress: Required - in Docker enter the address of the Docker host
headerSearchInstructions: How to enter it on the module
textSearch: The search asks once via mDNS and reads the settings page of each module (read only, nothing is changed). In Docker (bridge network) mDNS does not reach the modules - check a single address instead.
helpSearchTarget: Checks only this address - no range scan
textBind: Sets the MQTT host of ONE module to this adapter (address for modules : broker port). Choose the module, click Check, read the preview, then Connect. The module restarts and must report here within 90 s. Restore writes the previous MQTT host back. Only the MQTT host is changed (plus MQTT user/password if this adapter has a user) - no firmware, no other settings.
helpBindIp: Connected modules and hits of the search. Empty? Search first or check an address.
textBindAdresseFehlt: “Check” stays grey until the “Address for modules” at the top of this tab is filled in – without it the module would not know where to connect.
labelBindPass: Settings password of the module (if set)
helpBindPass: Used only for this one action - never saved
helpBindOtherOk: The module currently reports to another MQTT broker and will stop doing so
confirmBindText: The MQTT host of the module shown in the preview will be changed and the module restarts. Continue?
confirmBackText: The MQTT host read before Connect is written back and the module restarts. Continue?
labelVortagZuschlag: Margin on top of yesterday (percentage points)
textProbeAn: Dry run: the adapter only calculates. It shows everything but sends no command to the units. Switch the dry run off to go live. Applies after “Save”.
textProbeAus: Live: the adapter sends commands – to every unit whose own dry-run switch (data point regulation.demand.dryRun) is off as well. Applies after “Save”.
textRegelGeraete: One entry per air conditioner. A unit without an entry uses the defaults: the adapter controls, sensors on automatic.
textRegelAufklappen: → Click a row to expand the settings of that unit. The “+” adds an entry for another unit.
textBetriebAdapter: The adapter switches by weekly schedule and scenes, limits the power by demand and steps in on humidity. Every decision is shown as “reason” on the device card.
textBetriebFaikout: The module itself controls to the target temperature (automatic mode of the firmware). The adapter supplies target, sensor value and weekly schedule and still limits the power if the unit supports it.
textFuehler: “Automatic” takes the best available sensor. A BLE sensor on the module always has priority – the firmware defines that. If a value is too old, the adapter calculates without it and says so on the card.
helpFrostAb: 0 = off. Below this room temperature the adapter heats to 10 °C – even if the schedule says off.
textBedarf: Limits the power of the unit in 5 % steps so that it runs evenly instead of cycling. From 2 K below the target the adapter always releases 100 %. Switched on per unit on the device card.
textVortag: This is how “Auto” in the Daikin app works as well: yesterday’s power plus a reserve. Without data from yesterday the adapter releases 100 %.
helpTotband: Up to this difference between room and target the room does not change the power limit. Larger = calmer.
helpProzentProK: Percentage points added to (room too cold) or taken from (room too warm) the curve value per kelvin of difference beyond that. 0 = curve only.
labelBand: Target band for Faikout auto (± K)
helpBand: Only for units in mode “Faikout auto”: the module keeps the room within target ± this value.
textHand: If someone operates the unit at the device or in an app, schedule and scenes wait. Demand and humidity control keep working. “End manual override” on the device card ends the wait at once.
labelHandModus: After manual operation the automation waits
optHandNie: not at all (the schedule overrides at once)
textSzenen: A scene is a complete state of the unit. The weekly schedule switches between scenes. The cap limits the power in addition to the demand control. With an empty table the four default scenes apply: Komfort (21 °C), Absenken (19 °C), Abwesend (17 °C), Aus.
textSzenenSpalten: How the columns work together: “Max. power %” caps the power limit while the scene runs – the smaller value of curve and cap applies. If the room is 2 K or more behind the target, the control releases 100 % anyway. “Demand control” off = this scene runs without a power limit (100 %). “Humidity control” off = no humidity intervention during this scene.
textFeuchte: The closer the dew point gets to the room temperature, the muggier the air. This distance is the dew-point spread, ΔDP for short. If it falls below the limit or the humidity rises too high, the adapter steps in. Switched on per unit on the device card.
labelFeuchteMassnahme: What the adapter does when it is too humid
optMassZielSenken: Lower the target by 1 K when cooling
labelFeiertagSonntag: On public holidays the Sunday schedule applies
helpFeiertage: Dates separated by commas: 24.12. (every year), 31.12.2026 or 2026-12-31
headerModRead: Read and change settings in the module
textModRead: The adapter reads the settings from the module, shows the difference and only writes after your confirmation. Then it reads back and checks whether everything arrived.
helpModIp: All units of the adapter and the hits of the last search.
helpModReporting: reporting – seconds between two status messages
helpModLivestatus: livestatus – report every change at once
helpModThermostat: thermostat – the module switches hard on and off
helpModNodemand: nodemand – the module does not offer demand
confirmModText: The changes are listed in the preview (old → new). Every write wears the flash memory of the module and restarts it for some settings (about 10 s without connection). Afterwards the adapter reads back and shows the result per setting. The confirmation can take up to a minute – a module often shows a new value only after about 30 seconds. The symbol in the button spins while the adapter waits.
textRuht: Faikout auto with the strategy “curve”: demand control rests for this unit. With Faikout auto the power limit is only set with the strategy “Auto”.
headerVorgabe: Defaults for units without own values
textVorgabe: Curve, limits and scenes belong to each unit. Whatever is left empty at a unit is taken from here.
headerKopie: Take over values from another unit
textKopie: Copies scenes and/or curve from one unit entry to another. Takes effect at once: after the confirmation the unit list is saved and the adapter restarts.
confirmKopieTitle: Overwrite the values of the target unit?
confirmKopieText: The chosen values of the target unit are replaced and the unit list is saved at once; the adapter restarts. Other unsaved changes on this page are lost – save them first.
helpModAdresse: Only needed if the module does not report its address ("address not known yet") or is missing in the list.
helpModSicherung: Before every write the adapter keeps the state it read – the last five per module.
btnModRestore: Load this state into the form
labelFuehlerWeg: How the room data point takes effect
optWegModul: Send the sensor value to the module
textWegSollwert: The setpoint shown at the unit then differs from your target by the sensor correction (at most ±3 K). The target itself is named in the reason on the device card.
helpRaumTraege: 0 = off. Mixes in fast changes of the unit’s own sensor; only matters for the power limit and for “send to the module”.
labelKorrAbstand: Readjust at the earliest every … minutes
textModWait: The confirmation can take up to a minute – a module often shows a new value only after about 30 seconds. The symbol in the button spins while the adapter waits.
labelBrokerModus: Which broker do the modules use?
textBrokerIntern: The adapter brings its own MQTT broker. The faikout modules only have to point to it – nothing else needs to be installed.
textBrokerExtern: The adapter connects as a client to a broker you already run, for example Mosquitto or the ioBroker MQTT adapter. Its own broker does not run then and its port becomes free.
textBrokerWechsel: Switching loses no data: data points, weekly schedules and saved states stay. After saving, the adapter restarts.
textExternModule: The modules must point to the external broker themselves (module setting “mqtthost”) – the adapter does not change that automatically. Which modules still point to another broker is shown in the tab “Find modules” (column “Status”); there a module can also be switched over.
textExternZiel: External broker: the modules connect to your external broker from the tab "MQTT broker", not to this adapter. "Connect" switches the MQTT host of a module to the external broker.
labelExternHost: Address of the broker (IP or host name)
helpExternUser: Empty = sign in without user name
helpExternClientId: Name under which the adapter logs in at the broker. It must be unique: two clients with the same ID throw each other out again and again. The preset value was created once for this instance.
helpExternPraefix: Only if the modules publish below a prefix; usually empty
testOk: The broker is reachable and accepts the sign-in.
testAnmeldung: The broker answers, but rejects user name or password.
testNichtErreichbar: The broker is not reachable at this address and port.
testZeit: No answer from the broker in time (timeout).
testEingabe: Enter the address of the broker first.
headerSchritte: Three steps to your first unit
textSchritt1: Nothing to do if you do not run a broker of your own: the adapter brings its own MQTT broker. Only if you already use Mosquitto or similar, switch to "external" in the tab "MQTT broker".
textSchritt2: Tab "Find modules": click "Search", choose the module in the list and press "Connect". If ioBroker runs in Docker the search finds nothing – then check the address of the module under "Single address". By hand it works too: in the web interface of the module under Settings → Basic enter the value below at "MQTT host".
textSchritt2Extern: External broker: the modules have to point to your external broker, not to this adapter. Tab "Find modules": click "Search" – the column "Status" shows which module points where; "Connect" switches a module to the external broker. By hand: in the web interface of the module under Settings → Basic enter the value below at "MQTT host".
textSchritt3: Tab "Climate control": add one entry per unit, choose curve and sensors. You create the weekly schedule on the device card (button with the calendar); there you also switch power limit, humidity and schedule on. As long as "Dry run" is on, the adapter only calculates and sends nothing.
textBindExtern: Switches the MQTT host of ONE module to the external broker (address and port from the tab "MQTT broker", plus user and password if entered there). Choose a module, click "Check", read the preview, then "Connect". The module restarts and has to report via the external broker within 90 s. "Restore" writes the previous MQTT host back. Firmware and all other settings stay untouched.
textWegWahl: "Adjust setpoint": the unit keeps controlling itself, the adapter shifts its setpoint – also suitable for slow sensors in another room. "Send to module": the module controls the unit; it may cycle more often.
headerBrokerFortgeschritten: For advanced users: client ID and topic prefix
